name: Nebraska

law.summary: No Nebraska statute or rule found that requires public notice of a sewage overflow; Title 126's release rule covers oil and hazardous substances. Permittees report overflows and bypasses to DWEE and file them through EPA's NeT-SewerOverflow, which makes them public in EPA's daily extract. Omaha's CSO permit (NE0133680) presumably carries a Nine Minimum Controls notification clause, but its text was not reachable.

citations.title: Electronic sewer overflow and bypass event reports
citations.channel: EPA NeT-SewerOverflow (public via ECHO SOBE extract)

citations.title: Definition of SSO
citations.quote: "Sanitary Sewer Overflow (SSO)" means untreated or partially treated sewage overflows from a sanitary sewer collection system.

regulator_report.deadline: 24 hours oral, 5 days written (DWEE noncompliance form WAT098; inferred from standard conditions)
regulator_report.cite: Title 119 / NPDES permit standard conditions (not read)

bills_and_cases: Title 126 rewrite proposed 2026 (release notification moves to Chapter 1); not sewage-specific (search only).

erule.notes: 162 events from 21 permits, start dates 2022 to 2026-10-06; all with coordinates. Reporting coverage looks uneven (Lincoln 5, Omaha CSO 8).

statewide_feed.latency: start to receipt median 23 days (10% within 1 day; 10% over 83 days)

cso.notification_practice: Omaha: no web overflow notice found; announces major overflows through media. 8 Omaha CSO-permit events in SOBE. DMR event counts only at two treated outfalls (102, 205R).

beaches.program: DWEE Beach Watch: weekly E. coli and microcystin at about 56 public beach sites, mid-May to mid-September; health alert above 8 ug/L microcystin
beaches.notes: E. coli above 235/100 mL is reported but triggers no advisory.

habs.program: Same Beach Watch layer (microcystin health alerts, joint DWEE/DHHS)

outfalls.cso_inventory_gap: unknown (HDR describes 29 CSO points; EPA inventory has 25 open)

Big Blue and Little Blue rivers (KS)

readiness.rationale: EPA's SOBE extract carries event-level Nebraska reports with coordinates and volume (ingester exists); add the Beach Watch ArcGIS layer for beaches and HABs. Delay is long (median 23 days) and Omaha's CSO outfalls need the rain caution.

owner_questions: Accept a median 23-day delay for Nebraska's overflow reports, labelled 'Dated reports, delayed'?
Request Omaha's CSO public notification plan from the city or DWEE (records request)?
Subscribe to the Beach Watch listserv?
surprise: Omaha, the region's only big CSO city, has no web overflow notice found, yet its overflows (and Papillion Creek SSOs, 71 reports) are public with coordinates in EPA's daily extract, weeks late.
